BonaLabs: automatic Telegram news
================================

Status: prepared locally, not activated. The homepage shows three recent posts
from @BonaLabs once the bot starts receiving announcements. Until then, it shows
a direct channel link. No sample announcements are included in the public feed.

ONE-TIME SETUP (channel and repository owner)

1. Open the verified @BotFather account in Telegram and use /newbot.
   Create a new bot dedicated to this feed. Keep the token private.
   Official instructions: https://core.telegram.org/bots/features#botfather

2. Add that bot to the BonaLabs channel as an administrator. Disable optional
   posting, editing, deletion and invitation permissions where Telegram allows;
   this integration only reads channel posts. Do not connect this bot to another
   service that uses getUpdates or a webhook.

3. In the GitHub repository, Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions,
   add a repository secret named TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN containing the bot token.
   https://github.com/BonaLabs/bonalabs.github.io/settings/secrets/actions
   Never put the token in HTML, JavaScript, JSON, commits, issues or chat.

4. Push the reviewed website changes, including .github/, to main.
   No commit, push or deployment was performed when preparing this integration.

5. Settings > Pages > Build and deployment: select GitHub Actions as Source.
   Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > Variables: add repository
   variable TELEGRAM_FEED_ENABLED with value true.
   The workflow explicitly requests contents:write to save feed state; repository
   or organization policies and branch protection must allow its generated commits.

6. Actions > Telegram news and Pages > Run workflow. Check that build and deploy
   both finish successfully. Then publish the next normal announcement to the
   channel. The bot cannot import existing channel history. An empty feed on the
   first run is expected when no new post is available.

HOW IT WORKS

- GitHub checks Telegram at minutes 7, 22, 37 and 52 of each hour, on main pushes,
  and on manual runs. Scheduled jobs can be delayed; this is not real-time delivery.
- The synchronizer receives channel_post and edited_channel_post updates only.
  It filters the channel identity, extracts text and supported photos, groups
  albums, and stores a public snapshot in data/telegram-feed.json.
- The homepage displays three announcements with links to their original posts.
  It checks that local snapshot every five minutes while the tab is visible.
- Text, captions and rich-message text are supported. Photos are cached locally.
  Video, document and other attachments open on Telegram. A photo download error
  still allows the text and post link to appear.
- .github/telegram-state.json retains up to 40 normalized messages and the cursor;
  the public feed retains up to 12 posts. Neither contains bot credentials or raw
  updates. State is versioned, so pull main before making subsequent local changes.
- The workflow commits the snapshot and state before the next run acknowledges
  that batch. It then packages and deploys the public site in the same workflow.
- Packaging allows only public root files and articles/, icons/, assets/, data/.
  It excludes local-tools/, internal guidance, .github/ and preview screenshots.
- A failed synchronization stops the deployment; the already published website
  and its last news snapshot remain available. Inspect the failed Action and rerun
  it after fixing the cause. A bot with an existing webhook is rejected unchanged.
- Telegram retains pending updates for at most 24 hours. Downtime longer than that
  can lose announcements. GitHub can disable scheduled workflows after 60 days
  without repository activity; check Actions if the feed stops updating.
- Telegram does not provide ordinary channel-deletion updates through this API.
  To hide a removed post, add its numeric message ID to
  .github/telegram-hidden-posts.json, for example [39, 42], then push or run the
  workflow. Hiding one album member hides that album. Edits update automatically
  when Telegram delivers the edited-channel-post event.
- Old announcements need a separate historical import; this setup starts with
  posts received after the dedicated bot joins the channel.

LOCAL CHECKS

  python -m unittest discover -s .github/tests -v
  node --check telegram-news.js
  python .github/scripts/build_public_site.py

The packaging command requires an empty _site/ output directory.
Do not run the synchronizer locally against the live bot while Actions is active;
only one consumer should own its update queue.

References:
https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#getupdates
https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#update
https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq
https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/using-custom-workflows-with-github-pages
https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#schedule
